wallpapers.title: EARTHSET
wallpapers.line1: Earth sinks behind the Moon's Ohm crater, seen through Orion's window. Clouds over Australia on the day side.

wallpapers.title: EARTHRISE
wallpapers.line1: Earth rising over the Moon's horizon on Christmas Eve. On Earth, the sunset line crosses Africa.

wallpapers.title: CRESCENT MOON
wallpapers.line1: The Moon behind them on the way home. Low sunlight along the edge of night throws long shadows.

wallpapers.title: THE EDGE OF TWO WORLDS
wallpapers.line1: A crescent Earth six minutes before it passes behind the Moon. The rows of small pits are chains of secondary craters.

wallpapers.title: THE TERMINATOR
wallpapers.line1: The line between lunar day and night. Low sunlight casts long shadows that show how deep each crater is.

wallpapers.title: HADLEY DELTA
wallpapers.line1: Dave Scott studies a boulder on the slope of Hadley Delta. The Lunar Roving Vehicle stands on the right.
wallpapers.line2: Apollo 15, photo by Jim Irwin  ·  31 July 1971  ·  NASA

wallpapers.title: THE MOON FROM ORION
wallpapers.line1: More than two-thirds of the Moon. The dark round spot is Grimaldi crater; Orientale basin sits on the edge.

wallpapers.title: ORIENTALE BASIN
wallpapers.line1: The rings of one of the Moon's youngest and best-kept large impact craters, about 965 km (600 miles) wide.
